newsitem.title: UK: ICI slammed over leak and oil spill.
newsitem.headline: ICI slammed over leak and oil spill.

text.p: Britain's official environmental watchdog, the Environment Agency, on Thursday slammed Imperial Chemical Industries Plc for allegedly "outrageous" behaviour involving two new leaks at its plants.
ICI responded by saying it regretted the incidents and had taken immediate action to contain the leaks.

The Environment Agency said it had forced ICI to close down part of its Tioxide plant near Hartlepool in northeast England after a toxic cloud of titanium tetrachloride was released into the air on Wednesday evening.

"It is outrageous that within weeks of ICI being called to a meeting with the agency, where it promised to clean up its act, that its plants have been involved in two further leaks," the agency's head, Archie Robertson, said in a statement.
The agency said the road alongside the plant was closed and local residents were warned to close windows and stay indoors. Tioxide is a pigment used in paints.
ICI said in a statement that the incident did not cause any injuries and added that affected areas would remain shut down until it was satisfied that there would be no recurrences.
"We have already carried out preliminary investigations to discover the causes of the incidents, and we have kept the Environment Agency fully informed at every stage," ICI said.
About five hours after the leak at the Hartlepool plant, the agency was informed by ICI of an oil spill at its refinery in Wilton.

"These two incidents come just weeks after the Environment Agency called senior ICI executives to a meeting to discuss a series of pollution incidents at sites in the North East and North West," the agency said.
The Environment Agency said it would not allow the section of the Hartlepool plant responsible for the toxic gas leak to reopen until it was satisfied ICI would operate it safely.
"This is not the first leak of this material from this plant so we felt justified in taking this action, because ICI have had opportunities to put it right and have failed to do so," Robertson said.
In the second incident, the agency said, an unspecified amount of light gasoline was spilled into the Wilton site's drainage system and into the Tees estuary following routine maintenance.
It said an oil boom stopped the oil from polluting the estuary, adding that there had been six other serious incidents at ICI plants in the north of England since last July.
